post_text: “How do you get ideas for posts?” People ask me this a lot, here's how: 1. I have a doc where I store ideas throughout the day/week, not full drafts, just a quick note on the idea for the specific post. 2. I take lots of pictures, especially for LinkedIn this is helpful since they seem to boost posts with photos. 3. pull from different buckets. Personal life, work life, humor, learnings, experiences/stories, hot takes/beliefs. 4. start small. If you have a full time job, you probably don't have an hour/day to write a LinkedIn post. I started with posting 3 times a week and eventually ramped it up to more. 5. be consistent, pick a number and commit to it. 6. follow cool people, I get a lot of inspiration for posts from seeing what other people are doing on here. This is what I've picked up from posting consistently on here for the past year (ish). At the end of the day, there's pretty much zero downside and unlimited upside to posting on here.

All the LinkedIn “personal branding” growth advice is bs, here's the real sauce... I went from 0 to 2.6M LinkedIn impressions in a year by posting <35 posts. When I first started posting, I had NO clue what to write. I would literally find ANY posts that did well, copy them, feed them into ChatGPT, and be like “write me something like this based on ur knowledge of me”. It was bad. Eventually, I stopped copying and started understanding why things worked. That's how I built taste. My biggest lesson: don't try to become a better writer. Become better at recognizing what's interesting.

My post got taken down from Reddit 3 times today. I wasn't promoting or selling anything, just showcasing something I built. Didn't name any brands either. If you have any Reddit tips or tricks, I am all ears. Its a mystery for me but fun to explore. But like running or the gym, it is the same for posting. Consistency counts so I'll just keep trying.
